description: Trigger discrimination for the Phase 7 threat & injection cluster: hidden-context contents and secrecy-dependence (system prompt, developer instructions, retrieved policy text, tool/function schemas) vs injection defense vs user-data disclosure vs retrieval authorization vs tool-permission design vs credential custody vs persistent-memory poisoning vs context-assembly design vs inter-agent channels.

cases.prompt: Is it a problem that our security relies on the system prompt staying secret, and that the prompt has our internal endpoints in it?
cases.reason: Secrets in the prompt and dependence on prompt secrecy is this skill (LLM08); prompt-injection-defender is the input side and sensitive-disclosure-guard covers user/context data, not the application's hidden context.

cases.prompt: A user got our agent to print its full tool list and parameter schemas, including an admin-only export tool and a description that says the caller must be a developer. What did that expose and what should change?
cases.reason: Disclosure of tool schemas and reliance on a role rule written in a tool description is hidden context exposure (LLM08); agent-tool-safety-guard designs the permission matrix and would receive the routed enforcement fix, but does not own what the schema reveals.

cases.prompt: Our assistant loads our internal escalation policy from the knowledge base into its instructions, and users can get it to recite the thresholds. Is that a leak we need to fix?
cases.reason: Retrieved policy text placed in hidden context and echoed back is LLM08; rag-security-architect owns who may retrieve which documents and sensitive-disclosure-guard owns regulated user data, neither the application's own control text.

cases.prompt: Make sure a user's RAG search only returns documents their tenant and role are allowed to read, with ACLs applied in the vector query.
cases.reason: Authorization at retrieval time over access-controlled documents is rag-security-architect (LLM09); this skill reviews hidden policy text once it is in context, not document access control.

cases.prompt: Design least-privilege permissions for our agent's tools: which tools each role may call, argument validation, and approval before refunds.
cases.reason: Per-tool permission matrices, argument validation, and approval gates are agent-tool-safety-guard (LLM03); this skill only asks what tool schemas reveal and whether their text is relied on as a gate.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke prompt-injection-defender. Stop untrusted document content from overriding our agent's instructions at runtime.
cases.reason: Preventing untrusted content from changing behavior is prompt-injection-defender (manual-only); this skill reviews hidden context's contents and whether security wrongly depends on its secrecy.

cases.prompt: Make sure the model doesn't leak PII or another user's data in its responses.
cases.reason: Sensitive user/context/output data leakage is sensitive-disclosure-guard (LLM02); LLM08 excludes user and training data and covers the application's hidden control context.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke secrets-identity-hardener. Rotate the leaked key and set up proper server-side secret storage and least-privilege service accounts.
cases.reason: The custody/rotation mechanics are secrets-identity-hardener; this skill finds the secret in hidden context and routes it there, but doesn't own secret storage design.

cases.prompt: Our agent auto-saves conversation summaries to long-term memory and a poisoned note keeps resurfacing across sessions.
cases.reason: Persistent memory is an agentic amplification that LLM08 explicitly excludes; memory-context-poisoning-reviewer owns memory write, provenance, and recall controls. This skill reviews what hidden context contains and whether security relies on its secrecy.

cases.prompt: Design which fields and segments our context assembler includes under caps and closed schemas.
cases.reason: Choosing what enters the context window, under size caps and closed schemas, is model-context-designer's design work; this skill reviews the assembled hidden context for secrets and secrecy-dependence after the design exists.

cases.prompt: Our planner agent passes instructions to worker agents over a message bus; review whether a compromised worker can forge or tamper with those messages.
cases.reason: Authenticity and integrity of messages between agents is inter-agent-comms-reviewer; inter-agent channels are an agentic amplification outside LLM08 scope.
